quotes.quote: Step onto the platform or kneel on the pad. Grip the handles (most machines have multiple grip options—start with a shoulder-width, pronated/overhand grip). Ensure your knees or legs are securely positioned on the pad. Your body should be hanging freely, arms fully extended, core engaged.

Grip the bar with a pronated grip (palms facing away from you), a little wider than shoulder-width apart. Put your feet/knees on the pad and let your body weight push it down until you’re hanging with your arms extended.
Your chest should be proud, shoulders engaged, and core tight. This is a position of strength, not a collapsed hunch.
Keep your chest up, and look up at the bar.
Inhale and pull yourself up until your chin is over the bar or the bar touches your upper chest.
Exhale and lower yourself with control until your arms are fully extended again.
Continue pulling until your chin clears the bar.
Take 3-4 seconds to return to a dead hang.
This machine uses counterweight to offset a portion of your bodyweight. If you select 50 lbs of assistance, you are effectively lifting (your bodyweight - 50 lbs).
A higher plate weight means less load on your muscles.
Choose the lowest assistance weight that still allows you to complete 3–5 controlled reps with good form.
If you can't complete one rep without swinging, increase the assistance slightly.
Apply progressive overload deliberately, more reps, less assistance, then added load
Reducing the assistance weight over time is a sign of real progress.
Initiate the movement by pulling your shoulder blades down and back
Then, drive with your elbows, pulling them down towards your ribs.
Set the scapulae first, cueing 'pull the shoulder blades down and back' before the arms take over
The Partial Rep: Not going to a full dead hang or not pulling high enough.
The Swing: Using leg drive or momentum.
The Shrug: Initiating the pull with your shoulders up by your ears.
Discourage the common faults: kipping and momentum on strict-strength work, partial range of motion (coach a full hang at the bottom to a chin-clearing top), and craning the neck.
Take 3-4 seconds to return to a dead hang.
Briefly pause.
High arm elevation during pull-ups reduces sub-acromial space and increases pressure, increasing the risk of impingement injury.
